figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Biocatalytic strategies to access organic azides. (a) Azidooxygenation of alkenes. (b) Engineered metalloenzymes enabled radical
azidation mainly through a key radical rebound pathway. (c) Introducing azido group via natural enzymatic nonradical mechanisms. (d) This work:
enantioselective azidooxygenation of alkenes by direct visible-light-excited ene-reductase. Tri 17 = a promiscuous ATP- and nitrite-dependent
enzyme reported in ref 20, NPhth = phthalimide, FMN = flavin mononucleotide, FMNox = oxidation form of FMN, FMNox* = excited state
FMNox, and SET = single-electron transfer.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Development of photoenzymatic azidooxygenation of alkenes. (a) Evaluation of the key reaction parameters. (b) Active site image with
3a docked and the three mutated amino acid residues highlighted. (c) Evolution trajectory of PETNr. aConditions: 1a (0.005 mmol), 2 (0.01
mmol), NaN3 (0.02 mmol), ERED (1.0 mol%), DMSO (5 v/v %) in HEPES (50 mM, pH 7.5) were stirred at room temperature for 12 h under N2
atmosphere with the irradiation of blue LEDs. The total volume of the reaction mixture is 1 mL. bYield was determined by HPLC. cEnantiomeric
ratio (e.r.) was determined by HPLC analysis on a chiral stationary phase. n.d. = not determined, PETNr = ene-reductase fromEnterobacter cloacae.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. The scope of photoenzymatic azidooxygenation. The standard conditions shown in Figure 2a, entry 5, were applied. Yields were
determined by HPLC as the average of duplicates using two different batches of the enzyme. e.r.= enantiomeric ratio was determined by HPLC
analysis on a chiral stationary phase. aPETNr-M3 (2.0 mol%). bIndicates the isolated yield based on a 0.1 mmol scale-up reaction. Absolute
configuration was assigned based on the single-crystal structures of 4a (see Figure S3, Table S14 for more information).
